parameters.name: city_id
parameters.description:
**City id  -  the region whose sellers, stock and delivery times you want.** Optional; defaults to
`750000000` (Almaty).

The region scopes seller availability, stock and delivery promises, and should be kept consistent
when comparing results across calls.

Representative city ids:
**Observed behavior when changing cities:**

- **Delivery promise  -  can change substantially.** The same product may be `EXPRESS` in Almaty
  but `TILL_5_DAYS` or `TILL_7_DAYS` in a smaller city. This is the main reason to set `cityId`.
- **Seller set  -  can change slightly.** The available offers may differ between cities, so the
  competitive field should not be assumed to be identical.
- **Price  -  generally unchanged in testing.** Across sampled products and cities, listed prices
  (including the buy-box price) were identical. Do not assume city-specific price differences
  without checking the product.
- **Result counts  -  unchanged in testing.** The same keyword returned the same number of matches
  across the tested cities.

- `750000000`  -  Almaty (default)
- `710000000`  -  Astana
- `511010000`  -  Shymkent

All published cities and towns, with names in English, Russian and Kazakh plus map bounds, come from
`/cities`; `/city-details` adds the delivery-zone polygon for one of them.

**Send the id, not the name.** Every id is exactly nine digits. A city name, a truncated id or an id
not published by `/cities` is rejected with a `400` on **every** endpoint that takes a city.

description: The category tree to a chosen depth (0 - 5)  -  the source of the category codes used by search. Depth 1 - 2 is interactive; 3+ is a batch job.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description:
**Which navigation tree to fetch.** Optional; defaults to `catalog-categories`.

- `catalog-categories`  -  the full product catalogue (the default; its top-level `code`s are what
  `/search-products` accepts as `category`)
- `desktop-categories`  -  the shorter tree shown in the storefront's desktop side menu
- `desktop-topbar`  -  the horizontal top navigation bar on desktop
- `desktop-footer`  -  the link groups in the desktop page footer
- `mobile-footer`  -  the equivalent footer tree for the mobile site

Only `catalog-categories` carries codes usable as a search `category` filter  -  the other four
are storefront chrome (promotional links, informational pages) and mostly do not correspond to
sellable product categories.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description:
**How many levels below the requested node to return.** Optional; defaults to `2`.

Depths:

- `0`  -  just the requested node itself, no children (a quick existence check)
- `1`  -  one level of subcategories
- `2`  -  the default, typically enough to reach real product categories
- `3` - `5`  -  progressively deeper branches; `5` is the hard ceiling. Anything above `5` is
  rejected with a `400`

**Use `1` - `2` for interactive requests.** Depth `3` and beyond can exceed a 60-second client
timeout. For a deep branch, request that branch by `code` at a shallow depth instead of requesting
the whole catalogue deeply.

description: Search-as-you-type suggestions: completed query terms plus the categories each one leads to.

parameters.name: term
parameters.description:
**Partial search term to complete.** Required  -  a single word or the start of a phrase, in
Russian, Kazakh or English (the catalogue is trilingual).

Example: `iphon` returns next-word completions (`air`, `17`, `16`, `13`, `15`) plus full
suggestions such as `iphone 17 air` and `iphone 16 pro`, each tagged with the category it leads to.

This is intended for live, keystroke-by-keystroke lookups  -  pair it with a short client-side
debounce rather than calling it on every keypress. It is unrelated to `/search-products`: this
endpoint never returns products, only completed query terms and the categories behind them.

description: Every attribute filter available for a query, each with its product count and the exact value to send back.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description:
**Free-text search query.** Matches product titles, brands and model names, in Russian, Kazakh
or English  -  the catalogue is trilingual and a Latin-script query finds Cyrillic-titled products.

Examples: `iphone`, `samsung`, `наушники` (headphones),
`ноутбук` (laptop), `Apple iPhone 17 256Gb`, `моторное масло`.

**Send `text`, `category`, or both  -  at least one is required.** A search with neither is rejected
with a `400`. Sending both intersects the free-text query with the category.

Matching is relevance-based rather than literal, so a broad word returns a broad set. Combine it
with `category` to pin the result set to one product type. Use `/search-filters` to inspect the
exact total and available filters before paging with `/search-products`.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description:
**Category code to scope the search to**  -  use it to browse a whole product type.

Examples: `Smartphones`, `Smartphones and gadgets`,
`Notebooks`, `TV`, `Beauty`. Codes are English-language slugs even though the displayed category
names are Russian/Kazakh.

**Matching is case-insensitive**  -  `smartphones` and `Smartphones` are identical.

**Send `text`, `category`, or both  -  at least one is required.** A search with neither is rejected
with a `400`. Sending both intersects the free-text query with the category.

Get the full code tree from `/categories`; `/search-filters` also returns the category branch that
the current query sits in, which lets you discover the code for a query you already
have. Combining `category` with `text` intersects the two; adding `brand` narrows it further.

**Pair `category` with any price window.** A price band on its own can relax
the keyword match rather than return nothing (see `price_min`); a category clause pins the result
set to the product type so that cannot happen quietly.

parameters.name: price_min
parameters.description:
**Minimum price, in Kazakhstani tenge (₸).** Whole tenge, no decimals, no separators  -  send
`100000`, not `100 000` or `1000.00`.

Examples: `20000` for ₸20,000, `100000` for ₸100,000, `300000` for ₸300,000.

Send `price_min` alone for "at least", `price_max` alone for "at most", or both for a window  - 
the missing bound is filled in for you.

**The trap: when nothing matching `text` fits the band, the marketplace relaxes the KEYWORD rather
than returning zero.** The price window is always honoured  -  every card really is inside it  -  but
the products stop being what you searched for.

For example, a low `price_max` with `text=iphone` can return accessories and other unrelated products
inside the requested price band.

**Pin it with `category`.** For example, add `category=Smartphones` to keep a phone price search
inside smartphones; if no matching products fit the band, the result is empty.

The tell is the total: a count that jumps far **above** the unfiltered baseline means the keyword
was relaxed. Confirm a new price window with `/search-filters` before paging it.

The price this filters on is the region's cash list price, not the discounted-with-bonus figure
that also appears on each product, so a product can pass the filter and still display a lower
bonus-adjusted number.

`price_min=0` means "no lower bound".

parameters.name: facets
parameters.description:
**Advanced attribute filter  -  the escape hatch for anything the named filters do not cover.**
Optional; unset means no extra constraint.

It takes one or more raw filter clauses in the form `::`, concatenated with no
separator, and they combine with **AND**  -  every extra clause narrows the result set.

Examples:
- `:Smartphones*Internal memory size:256 ГБ`  -  256 GB models
- `:Smartphones*Internal memory size:128 ГБ`  -  128 GB models
- `:Smartphones*Smartphone RAM size:8 ГБ`  -  8 GB RAM
- `:Smartphones*Series:Apple iPhone 14`  -  one model line
- `:Smartphones*Colour:белый:Smartphones*5G:true`  -  two clauses combined (white **and** 5G)

**Never hand-write a clause.** Call `/search-filters` for your query and paste a value straight
from it  -  each option there is returned with the exact clause to send and the number of products
behind it, so you can see its expected effect. Facet ids are category-specific
(a smartphone attribute means nothing in a tyre search) and many values are Cyrillic, including
the units (`ГБ` = GB, `мАч` = mAh).

**An unrecognised clause is ignored rather than rejected**, so a typo looks like a working filter
that simply did not narrow anything. Confirm with `/search-filters` that the total moved.

parameters.name: city_id
parameters.description:
**City id  -  the region whose sellers, stock and delivery times you want.** Optional; defaults to
`750000000` (Almaty).

The region scopes seller availability, stock and delivery promises, and should be kept consistent
when comparing results across calls.

Representative city ids:
**Observed behavior when changing cities:**

- **Delivery promise  -  can change substantially.** The same product may be `EXPRESS` in Almaty
  but `TILL_5_DAYS` or `TILL_7_DAYS` in a smaller city. This is the main reason to set `cityId`.
- **Seller set  -  can change slightly.** The available offers may differ between cities, so the
  competitive field should not be assumed to be identical.
- **Price  -  generally unchanged in testing.** Across sampled products and cities, listed prices
  (including the buy-box price) were identical. Do not assume city-specific price differences
  without checking the product.
- **Result counts  -  unchanged in testing.** The same keyword returned the same number of matches
  across the tested cities.

- `750000000`  -  Almaty (default)
- `710000000`  -  Astana
- `511010000`  -  Shymkent

All published cities and towns, with names in English, Russian and Kazakh plus map bounds, come from
`/cities`; `/city-details` adds the delivery-zone polygon for one of them.

**Send the id, not the name.** Every id is exactly nine digits. A city name, a truncated id or an id
not published by `/cities` is rejected with a `400` on **every** endpoint that takes a city.

text.description:
**Free-text search query.** Matches product titles, brands and model names, in Russian, Kazakh
or English  -  the catalogue is trilingual and a Latin-script query finds Cyrillic-titled products.

Examples: `iphone`, `samsung`, `наушники` (headphones),
`ноутбук` (laptop), `Apple iPhone 17 256Gb`, `моторное масло`.

**Send `text`, `category`, or both  -  at least one is required.** A search with neither is rejected
with a `400`. Sending both intersects the free-text query with the category.

Matching is relevance-based rather than literal, so a broad word returns a broad set. Combine it
with `category` to pin the result set to one product type. Use `/search-filters` to inspect the
exact total and available filters before paging with `/search-products`.

category.description:
**Category code to scope the search to**  -  use it to browse a whole product type.

Examples: `Smartphones`, `Smartphones and gadgets`,
`Notebooks`, `TV`, `Beauty`. Codes are English-language slugs even though the displayed category
names are Russian/Kazakh.

**Matching is case-insensitive**  -  `smartphones` and `Smartphones` are identical.

**Send `text`, `category`, or both  -  at least one is required.** A search with neither is rejected
with a `400`. Sending both intersects the free-text query with the category.

Get the full code tree from `/categories`; `/search-filters` also returns the category branch that
the current query sits in, which lets you discover the code for a query you already
have. Combining `category` with `text` intersects the two; adding `brand` narrows it further.

**Pair `category` with any price window.** A price band on its own can relax
the keyword match rather than return nothing (see `price_min`); a category clause pins the result
set to the product type so that cannot happen quietly.

price_min.description:
**Minimum price, in Kazakhstani tenge (₸).** Whole tenge, no decimals, no separators  -  send
`100000`, not `100 000` or `1000.00`.

Examples: `20000` for ₸20,000, `100000` for ₸100,000, `300000` for ₸300,000.

Send `price_min` alone for "at least", `price_max` alone for "at most", or both for a window  - 
the missing bound is filled in for you.

**The trap: when nothing matching `text` fits the band, the marketplace relaxes the KEYWORD rather
than returning zero.** The price window is always honoured  -  every card really is inside it  -  but
the products stop being what you searched for.

For example, a low `price_max` with `text=iphone` can return accessories and other unrelated products
inside the requested price band.

**Pin it with `category`.** For example, add `category=Smartphones` to keep a phone price search
inside smartphones; if no matching products fit the band, the result is empty.

The tell is the total: a count that jumps far **above** the unfiltered baseline means the keyword
was relaxed. Confirm a new price window with `/search-filters` before paging it.

The price this filters on is the region's cash list price, not the discounted-with-bonus figure
that also appears on each product, so a product can pass the filter and still display a lower
bonus-adjusted number.

`price_min=0` means "no lower bound".

Examples: `50000` for ₸50,000, `300000` for ₸300,000, `1000000` for ₸1,000,000.

parameters.name: sort

- `price-asc`  -  cheapest first
- `price-desc`  -  most expensive first
- `created-desc`  -  newest listings first (a new-arrivals feed)
- `rating`  -  highest customer rating first

These five are the complete accepted set.

Sorting is applied across the whole matching set, not just the current page, so `price-asc` with
`page=0` really is the cheapest twelve. It does not change the number of matches  -  only their
order  -  so the total reported by `/search-filters` is identical for every sort.

on a page are not strictly ordered by the `createdTime` field this API
returns. Treat it as a new-arrivals feed, and re-sort on `createdTime` yourself if you need an
exact chronological sequence.

parameters.name: facets
parameters.description:
**Advanced attribute filter  -  the escape hatch for anything the named filters do not cover.**
Optional; unset means no extra constraint.

It takes one or more raw filter clauses in the form `::`, concatenated with no
separator, and they combine with **AND**  -  every extra clause narrows the result set.

Examples:
- `:Smartphones*Internal memory size:256 ГБ`  -  256 GB models
- `:Smartphones*Internal memory size:128 ГБ`  -  128 GB models
- `:Smartphones*Smartphone RAM size:8 ГБ`  -  8 GB RAM
- `:Smartphones*Series:Apple iPhone 14`  -  one model line
- `:Smartphones*Colour:белый:Smartphones*5G:true`  -  two clauses combined (white **and** 5G)

cap and the count you sent rather than quietly answering for the first 150.

The response reports every requested code split into `inStock` and `outOfStock`. A code you never
asked about never appears in either list.

**Restrict the check to specific sellers**, comma-separated, taking their opaque, case-sensitive
merchant uids (e.g. `Satel`, `30027560`) rather than display names. Optional; unset checks

"does this exist". The match is exact and case-sensitive  -  `satel` finds nothing where `Satel`
does  -  and an id that is not a real seller simply matches nothing rather than erroring. Comma-separated.

product_codes.description:

cap and the count you sent rather than quietly answering for the first 150.

The response reports every requested code split into `inStock` and `outOfStock`. A code you never
asked about never appears in either list.

parameters.name: latitude
parameters.description:
**Latitude of the point to find the nearest pickup points to.** Optional; omit for the plain city
listing. Must be paired with `longitude`  -  a `latitude` sent alone is ignored and the city listing
is returned instead.

point carries a `distanceKm`. Without them `distanceKm` is `null` on every point and the city's own
order is kept.

With coordinates, `limit=1&offset=0` returns only the nearest point. Larger ranked requests can take
long enough to require an extended client timeout; see `limit`.

- `1`  -  with coordinates, the single nearest point
- `10`  -  a quick "what is nearby" check
- `50`  -  the default, a full screen of results
- `200`  -  the hard ceiling; anything above it is rejected with a `400`

Without coordinates, the city listing is sliced to `limit`, with the true `total`
reported alongside so you know how much more there is to page.

description: Seller profile with headline rating, review count, sales-volume band, legal address and opening hours.

parameters.name: merchant_id
parameters.description:
**Merchant id  -  the marketplace uid of one seller.** Required.

It is an **opaque string, not a number.** Real values include `Satel`, `SuperPrice`, `Berekekz`,
`30027560` and `16552044`  -  some sellers have a numeric uid, others an alphabetic one, so always
carry it as text and never parse it to an integer.

**It is case-sensitive**: `Satel`
resolves, `SATEL` and `satel` return `404`. Copy it verbatim.

Where to get one:
- `/sellers-by-keyword` → `merchantId` (it also ranks sellers by
  how many products they list for a keyword)
- `/product-offers` → `offers[].merchantId`, and `buyBox.merchantId` for the current cheapest seller

**Do not use a product card's `bestMerchantName`.** That field is a display name (`Sulpak`), not an
id  -  passing it here will usually 404. `/product-offers` is the only place the real buy-box id lives.

The same id is accepted by `/merchant-details`, `/merchant-quality-score`,
`/merchant-rating-summary`, `/merchant-reviews` and by the `merchant_id` search filter.

parameters.name: facets
parameters.description:
**Advanced attribute filter  -  the escape hatch for anything the named filters do not cover.**
Optional; unset means no extra constraint.

It takes one or more raw filter clauses in the form `::`, concatenated with no
separator, and they combine with **AND**  -  every extra clause narrows the result set.

Examples:
- `:Smartphones*Internal memory size:256 ГБ`  -  256 GB models
- `:Smartphones*Internal memory size:128 ГБ`  -  128 GB models
- `:Smartphones*Smartphone RAM size:8 ГБ`  -  8 GB RAM
- `:Smartphones*Series:Apple iPhone 14`  -  one model line
- `:Smartphones*Colour:белый:Smartphones*5G:true`  -  two clauses combined (white **and** 5G)

**Never hand-write a clause.** Call `/search-filters` for your query and paste a value straight
from it  -  each option there is returned with the exact clause to send and the number of products
behind it, so you can see its expected effect. Facet ids are category-specific
(a smartphone attribute means nothing in a tyre search) and many values are Cyrillic, including
the units (`ГБ` = GB, `мАч` = mAh).

**An unrecognised clause is ignored rather than rejected**, so a typo looks like a working filter
that simply did not narrow anything. Confirm with `/search-filters` that the total moved.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
**Result ordering.** Optional; defaults to `relevance`.

- `relevance`  -  best match first (the default; also what the marketplace shows as "Popular")
- `price-asc`  -  cheapest first
- `price-desc`  -  most expensive first
- `created-desc`  -  newest listings first (a new-arrivals feed)
- `rating`  -  highest customer rating first

These five are the complete accepted set.

Sorting is applied across the whole matching set, not just the current page, so `price-asc` with
`page=0` really is the cheapest twelve. It does not change the number of matches  -  only their
order  -  so the total reported by `/search-filters` is identical for every sort.

**One caveat on `created-desc`:** it surfaces recently-listed products, but the twelve results
on a page are not strictly ordered by the `createdTime` field this API
returns. Treat it as a new-arrivals feed, and re-sort on `createdTime` yourself if you need an
exact chronological sequence.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description:
**Page number, starting at `0`.** Optional; defaults to `0` (the first page).

**Pages are zero-based**  -  `page=0` is results 1 - 12, `page=1` is results 13 - 24, `page=2` is 25 - 36.
Sending `1` for the first page skips the first twelve results.

**Page size is fixed at 12 and cannot be changed**  -  there is no `limit` parameter. To collect 60
results, request pages `0` through `4`.

**Maximum page is `300`**  -  a deep window of 3,612 results. Page `301` and beyond is rejected with a
`400`. Paging past the end of a smaller result set simply returns an empty list, so use
`/search-filters` to learn the real total up front and page only as far as it justifies.

parameters.name: city_id
parameters.description:
**City id  -  the region whose sellers, stock and delivery times you want.** Optional; defaults to
`750000000` (Almaty).

The region scopes seller availability, stock and delivery promises, and should be kept consistent
when comparing results across calls.

Representative city ids:
**Observed behavior when changing cities:**

- **Delivery promise  -  can change substantially.** The same product may be `EXPRESS` in Almaty
  but `TILL_5_DAYS` or `TILL_7_DAYS` in a smaller city. This is the main reason to set `cityId`.
- **Seller set  -  can change slightly.** The available offers may differ between cities, so the
  competitive field should not be assumed to be identical.
- **Price  -  generally unchanged in testing.** Across sampled products and cities, listed prices
  (including the buy-box price) were identical. Do not assume city-specific price differences
  without checking the product.
- **Result counts  -  unchanged in testing.** The same keyword returned the same number of matches
  across the tested cities.

- `750000000`  -  Almaty (default)
- `710000000`  -  Astana
- `511010000`  -  Shymkent

All published cities and towns, with names in English, Russian and Kazakh plus map bounds, come from
`/cities`; `/city-details` adds the delivery-zone polygon for one of them.

**Send the id, not the name.** Every id is exactly nine digits. A city name, a truncated id or an id
not published by `/cities` is rejected with a `400` on **every** endpoint that takes a city.

description: Step through make, model and year to the tyre sizes that fit a vehicle.

parameters.name: mark
parameters.description:
**Vehicle make, to move from the make list to its model list.** Optional; omit every parameter
to get the make list itself.

Examples: `BMW`, `Toyota`, `Volkswagen`, `ВАЗ`.

This is a progressive picker, and every step is driven by how much you have already supplied:
no parameters → makes, `mark` alone → its models, `mark`+`model` → its years,
`mark`+`model`+`year` → the engine modifications and factory tyre sizes for that exact build.

**The response shape changes on the last step.** The first three steps return the candidate list
in `options[]`; the final step returns no `options` at all and instead carries `modifications[]`
(the engine variants of that build) and `tyreSizes[]` (the answer  -  each with `width`, `height`
and `diameter` split out) plus a `partialErrors[]` note if one of those two lookups failed on its
own. Read `step` (`marks` / `models` / `years` / `sizes`) to know which shape you are holding.

**Always send the `value` a previous step returned, never its `title`.** A make's `value` and
`title` happen to be identical (`BMW`), but a model's do not  -  see `model`.

description: Identify a vehicle from its VIN so parts can be matched to it.

parameters.name: vin
parameters.description:
**Vehicle Identification Number to decode.** Required  -  the 17-character VIN stamped on the
chassis or printed on the registration document.

Example: `1HGCM82633A004352` (a 2003 Honda Accord, USA-market EX-V6).

(trim, transmission, destination market)  -  because those variants can carry different part
numbers and tyre sizes even though they share a VIN prefix. Feed a result's `vehicleId` into the
automotive catalogue to match parts to it.

A VIN the catalogue has never indexed answers a clean `404` rather than an empty success.
